# Results — Study 900 (Quality-Income)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**chasing dividend YIELD selects value traps; screening dividends for QUALITY selects
durable payers, so a quality-dividend sleeve should beat a raw high-yield sleeve on
risk-adjusted terms** — raced as a live-product contest: quality sleeve (SCHD+NOBL) vs
yield sleeve (SPHD+VYM) vs SPY, all monthly total returns, all excess of cash (minus
BIL). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. Generated **2026-08-12**; monthly stats sliced **as-of 2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint
`bcc70b411b64`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted closes (**total-return**, dividends reinvested, net of fee) — SCHD, NOBL, VYM, SPHD, SPY, BIL |
| Sleeves | **Quality** = equal-weight SCHD+NOBL, monthly rebalance; **Yield** = equal-weight SPHD+VYM, monthly rebalance |
| Windows | Quality (NOBL-bound) 2013-11 → 2026-06 (**152** months); Yield 2012-11 → 2026-06 (164). **Common race window = 152 months** |
| Cash leg | **BIL** (SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill) — its monthly total return *is* the realized cash return; every Sharpe is excess of it |
| Execution / costs | buy-and-hold sleeves rebalanced monthly to equal weight; cost = one-way spread × realized turnover (≈0.6%/mo); long-only, no borrow; rebalance uses only within-month drift — no look-ahead |

> **Short-history / survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** All four sleeve ETFs are
> young — NOBL (2013-10) binds the common window — and they are *surviving* flagship
> products. The race therefore lives inside a single ~2013-2026 mostly-bull regime with
> only two real stress episodes (2020 COVID, 2022 rate shock). Magnitudes are an upper
> bound on the *average* dividend-ETF experience; the caveat travels with every number.

## The race (common window, 152 months; excess = minus BIL)

| sleeve | CAGR | ann vol | **excess Sharpe** | max drawdown | growth of $1 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **QUALITY** (SCHD+NOBL) | 11.00% | 13.9% | **0.697** | **−22.4%** | 3.75 |
| **YIELD** (SPHD+VYM) | 10.13% | 13.7% | 0.650 | −27.5% | 3.40 |
| SPY | 14.02% | 14.5% | **0.862** | −23.9% | 5.27 |

Quality out-earns yield by ~0.9 pp/yr with a **5-point-shallower drawdown** — but SPY
beats both by ~3-4 pp/yr of CAGR and ~0.17-0.21 of Sharpe.

## Headline — quality vs yield (the "does quality beat yield?" test)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| excess Sharpe gap (quality − yield) | **+0.047** |
| quality−yield monthly spread | +6.7 bps/mo (**+0.81%/yr**) |
| one-sample *t* on the spread | +0.77 |
| **Newey-West (HAC) *t*** on the spread | **+0.57** |
| paired block-bootstrap 95% CI on the gap | **[−0.191, +0.241]** |
| P(gap < 0) across 4,000 block draws | **0.355** |

The Sharpe advantage is **positive in sign but statistically indistinguishable from
zero**: the bootstrap CI straddles zero and one draw in three has quality *behind*. The
"quality wins on risk-adjusted return" claim does **not** clear the bar.

## Where quality genuinely wins — the drawdown / trap-avoidance channel

The real, mechanical part of the thesis shows up not in the Sharpe but in the **crisis
years**, exactly where yield-traps blow up:

| calendar year | QUALITY | YIELD | SPY | note |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 2018 | −4.4 | −6.0 | −4.6 | Q4 sell-off |
| 2019 | +27.4 | +22.2 | +31.2 | |
| **2020** | **+11.7** | **−4.7** | +18.3 | COVID — yield sleeve (SPHD) cratered |
| 2021 | +27.7 | +25.5 | +28.7 | |
| **2022** | **−4.9** | **+0.1** | −18.2 | rate shock — yield's low-vol screen cushioned |
| 2023 | +6.3 | +3.9 | +26.2 | AI-led cap-weight tape left both behind |
| 2024 | +9.2 | +17.9 | +24.9 | yield sleeve's turn |
| 2025 | +5.6 | +9.3 | +17.7 | |

*(2013 and 2026 are partial calendar years and omitted above.)* Quality dodged the 2020
yield-sleeve crater (+11.7% vs −4.7%), giving it the shallower max drawdown (−22.4% vs
−27.5%). But it is a two-way trade: yield's low-vol screen actually *won* 2022 and 2024.
The net Sharpe difference washes out — a real **drawdown cushion**, not a certified
return premium.

## Era cut (split 2020-01-01) — no stable magnitude

| era | months | Sharpe gap | quality−yield | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2013-11 → 2019-12 | 74 | −0.007 | +0.60%/yr | +0.46 |
| 2020-01 → 2026-06 | 78 | +0.060 | +1.00%/yr | +0.41 |

The gap is ~zero in the first era and a statistically-insignificant +0.06 in the second
— no era shows a significant quality-over-yield Sharpe premium.

## Do the sleeves beat SPY? — no (both lag)

| race | excess Sharpe | gap | diff | NW *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| quality vs SPY | 0.697 vs 0.862 | −0.165 | −2.81%/yr | −1.45 |
| yield vs SPY | 0.650 vs 0.862 | −0.212 | −3.62%/yr | −1.44 |

Both dividend sleeves **trail SPY** by ~3-4 pp/yr of return and ~0.17-0.21 of Sharpe over
the window (the 2023-24 cap-weighted-tech tape did most of the damage). The dividend
question is quality-vs-yield, not dividend-vs-market — on the latter, plain SPY won.

## Costs — negligible (buy-and-hold, cheap, no shorts)

| one-way spread | quality gross → net Sharpe | yield gross → net | drag |
|---|---|---|--:|
| 3 bps/side | 0.697 → 0.697 | 0.650 → 0.650 | 0.2 bps/yr |
| 10 bps/side | 0.697 → 0.696 | 0.650 → 0.650 | 0.7 bps/yr |

Monthly turnover is ~0.6%/mo (only the drift back to 50/50), so even a fat 10 bps spread
costs under 1 bp/yr. Costs do **not** move the verdict either way — the tilt is trivially
and cheaply buyable; there is simply no significant premium for the friction to erase.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic joint (market, quality, yield) monthly world, 150 months, all excess of
cash, with a TUNABLE planted quality-over-yield edge (`data.synthetic_world`):

| world | Sharpe gap | quality−yield | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), 20 seeds | ~0 | ~0 | mean −0.40 (sd 1.03), \|t\|≥2 in **1/20** |
| planted (edge = +3%/yr) | **+0.505** | +6.59%/yr | **+3.03** |

The gap detector stays quiet on the null and recovers a planted quality premium cleanly.
*(Machinery proof only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Screening dividends for quality *does* edge raw yield in the right
  direction: +0.9 pp/yr of CAGR, a Sharpe gap of **+0.047**, and — the genuinely
  mechanical part — a **5-point-shallower max drawdown (−22.4% vs −27.5%)** driven by
  dodging the 2020 yield-sleeve crater (+11.7% vs −4.7%). But the risk-adjusted edge is
  **not statistically distinguishable from zero**: NW *t* = **+0.57**, bootstrap 95% CI
  **[−0.19, +0.24]** straddles zero (P(gap<0) = 0.36), and no era shows a significant
  gap. The real payoff is a *drawdown cushion / trap-avoidance* profile, not a certified
  return premium — Weak, on a short single-regime tape.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The quality tilt is as buyable as it gets — SCHD/NOBL are
  cheap, liquid, one-ticket, long-only, and the monthly rebalance costs under 1 bp/yr, so
  nothing erases the tilt (not a Mirage). But there is no significant premium to bank:
  what you actually buy is a *shallower-drawdown risk profile*, not an edge, much like a
  min-vol wrapper. Real-but-thin and cheaply implementable → **Fragile**, not Investable.
- **"Beat SPY?" — no.** Both dividend sleeves trailed plain SPY by ~3-4 pp/yr and
  ~0.17-0.21 of Sharpe over 2013-2026. The honest answer to "does screening dividends for
  quality beat chasing yield?" is: *marginally, and mostly in drawdowns — but neither
  dividend approach beat just owning the market.*
